propositions: The live tickets branch .bridge_state/projects.json was corrupted with rehearsal fixture keys LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO (mapped to nonexistent Jira projects) instead of the canonical empty projects mapping, causing the multi-project fan-out to issue invalid JQL queries.

The fetcher multi-project fan-out (story-1734) iterates over every key in read_projects().keys(); when it encounters the nonexistent LEG key, jql_active constructs project = LEG AND status != Done, which Jira rejects with 'value leg does not exist for field project', causing ACLI to exit 1 and the entire reconcile pass to fail.

The corruption was introduced via ad-hoc git commits (9f1b2cff98 and 275bd7507e, authored by test-fixture identity) directly to origin/tickets at 2026-08-14T19:18-0700, 21 minutes before the first consistent Reconcile Bridge failure at 2026-08-15T02:39Z.

The bridge-state write path (_write_record via projects_store.set_project/remove_project) lacks the unified store write lock, commit, and publish semantics required by the store concurrency contract, enabling the ad-hoc hand-commits that leaked rehearsal state to production.

Restoration of origin/tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json to the canonical seed state {version:1, legacy_default:REB, projects:{}} and subsequent hardening fixes (fan-out resilience, preflight validation, atomic writes, write-lock adoption) resolved the outage and prevent recurrence.
